mainTopic: Selling an unborn animal, or only the rights to an animal's fetuses, to a non-Jew
overview: The גמרא asks whether רבי יהודה forbids selling an unborn animal (עובר) to a non-Jew, just as he forbids selling a large working animal. A ברייתא about a man fined for handing an animal to a non-Jew is pushed off: the fine is really about the mother animal. רב אשי then proves it from רבי יהודה's own reason. He allows selling a broken animal (שבורה) only because it can never heal and work. A fetus will work one day, so it is forbidden. A second version attaches this whole discussion to our משנה and reaches the same result. Next the גמרא asks a new question: may a Jew sell a non-Jew only the rights to an animal's fetuses? It works this out according to both רבי יהודה and the רבנן. A proof from the wording of our משנה is rejected. The amud ends by quoting a ברייתא of רבי יהודה and the חכמים about giving an animal to a non-Jew to raise, and the proof from it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Trying to read the ברייתא as talking about the fetus
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the ברייתא's 'he is not permitted to sell' refers to the עובר, which would prove that selling a fetus is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it talking about the fetus?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא has just quoted a ברייתא where someone is fined for selling to a non-Jew. Now it suggests that the forbidden sale there was the sale of the unborn animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ban and the fine are about the עובר, then selling a fetus to a non-Jew is forbidden. That would answer the open question. The phrase 'מאי לאו' signals a suggested reading that the גמרא may still push back on.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it? (opens a suggested proof-reading)
Unborn animal, a fetus

phrases.english: What, is it not referring to the fetus?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the ברייתא cited on the previous amud.
steps.raayaObject: Selling a עובר to a non-Jew is forbidden according to רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא that fines a seller who sold to a non-Jew.

steps.title: No, the ברייתא is about the mother animal
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The forbidden sale in the ברייתא is of the mother animal itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is referring to the animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof. The thing that 'may not be sold' is the full-grown mother animal, not the fetus.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Selling a full-grown large animal is clearly forbidden, so the ברייתא proves nothing about a fetus. The question about the עובר is settled later, by רב אשי's proof in step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: No (rejecting the suggested reading)
Animal; here, the mother animal

phrases.english: No, it is referring to the animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the reading of this ברייתא, not the possibility that a עובר is forbidden.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can just as easily be about the mother animal, which is clearly forbidden to sell.

steps.title: But the ברייתא says 'its value' in the masculine
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says 'דמיו' (masculine), which fits the עובר, not the mother animal (feminine).
steps.simpleTranslation: But it teaches 'its value' in the masculine!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 2 using the grammar of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בהמה' is a feminine word, so 'its value' for the mother should be 'דמיה'. The ברייתא's masculine 'דמיו' seems to point to the עובר, a masculine word. That undercuts the claim that the ברייתא is about the mother.

keyTerms.meaning: But it teaches! (introduces a challenge from the text)
Its value (masculine)

phrases.english: But doesn't it teach 'its value' (masculine)!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rejection in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא refers to the mother animal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The masculine pronoun fits עובר, not the feminine בהמה.

steps.title: Change the wording to 'its value' in the feminine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא amends the ברייתא to read 'דמיה' (feminine).
steps.simpleTranslation: Teach: 'its value' in the feminine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by changing one word of the ברייתא so it refers to the mother animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a text correction ('תני'). Once the word reads 'דמיה', the grammar fits the mother animal. The reading from step 2 survives.

keyTerms.meaning: Teach / read it as (a correction of the text)
Its value (feminine)

phrases.english: Teach: 'its value' (feminine).
phrases.notes: The גמרא is adjusting the wording here, so read it as 'her value', meaning the mother animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The masculine wording proves the ברייתא is about the עובר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The correct reading is feminine, so it refers to the mother animal.

steps.title: But the money goes to the כהן
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says all the value is given to the כהן. That only makes sense for a firstborn (בכור), not for an ordinary mother animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it teaches: 'he gives all its value to the כהן'. If it is about the mother animal, what does the כהן have to do with it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reading from step 2 again, this time from the content of the ברייתא rather than its grammar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן gets the firstborn (בכור) that comes out of the womb, not the mother. Since the ברייתא sends the money to the כהן, it seems to be about the fetus, which would become a בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: Priest, who receives the firstborn
What is his business here? What does he have to do with it?

phrases.english: But doesn't it teach: 'He gives all of its value to the priest',
and if it is about the animal,
what does the priest have to do with it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, stronger attack on the reading from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא is about the mother animal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only a firstborn goes to the כהן, so the money going to him shows the subject is the עובר.

steps.title: A pregnant animal given out for fattening
steps.stepSummary: The case is a pregnant animal given to a non-Jew to fatten. Since the man is fined for the mother, he is also fined for the fetus.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here we are dealing with someone who gave the non-Jew a pregnant animal to fatten. Since we fine him for the animal, we also fine him for the fetus.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the case so that the ברייתא is about the mother animal while still involving the כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real sin was handing over the mother animal, which is forbidden. Because of that, the חכמים extend the fine to the עובר as well, and that value goes to the כהן. This is a מיגו: since he is fined for one, he is fined for the other. So the fine on the fetus proves nothing about whether selling a fetus alone is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, what case are we dealing with? (narrows the case)
To fatten it
Since (because of one thing, another follows)
We penalize / fine

steps.confusionAlert: The fetus IS fined here, but only as a side effect of the forbidden handover of the mother. This does not prove that a fetus on its own is forbidden to sell.

phrases.english: Here, with what are we dealing?
For example, where he gave him
a pregnant animal to fatten it,
since we penalize him for the animal,
we penalize him for the fetus too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 5. The first proof attempt is now fully pushed off.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כהן's involvement shows that the forbidden sale was of the עובר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The forbidden act was handing over the mother. The fine on the fetus is only an extension of that.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a fine can spread from a forbidden act to something attached to it, without that attached item being forbidden on its own.

steps.title: רב אשי's proof from the broken animal
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה permits selling a broken animal because it can never heal. So one that can heal is forbidden, and a עובר is like one that can 'heal', since it will work one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Come and hear. רבי יהודה permits a broken animal, because it cannot heal. This implies that if it could heal, he would forbid it. And a fetus is like something that can heal.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings a new proof to answer the open question about the עובר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for the ban is that the animal could be used for work. רבי יהודה allows a broken animal only because it will never work. A fetus cannot work now but will in the future, just like an animal that will heal. So it should be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introduces a proof)
A broken / injured animal
To be healed
Is similar to

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: Come and hear,
Rabbi Yehuda permits a broken animal,
phrases.notes: Permits selling it to a non-Jew.

phrases.english: because it cannot be healed.
This implies: if it can be healed, he forbids it,
and a fetus too
is like something that can be healed.
phrases.notes: It will be able to work in the future.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof failed, רב אשי offers a new one.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה forbids selling a עובר to a non-Jew.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה's reason for permitting a broken animal (משנה in עבודה זרה).

steps.title: Conclusion: a fetus is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The proof stands. רבי יהודה forbids selling a עובר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts רב אשי's proof and closes this version of the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a fetus counts as something that will be able to work, it falls under the ban according to רבי יהודה. The open question is answered.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it (the proof is accepted)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, the test is whether the animal will ever be able to work. A broken animal never will, so it is permitted. A fetus will, so it is forbidden.

phrases.english: Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the proof of step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהודה forbids selling an unborn animal to a non-Jew.

steps.title: A second version, attached to our משנה
steps.stepSummary: Some place this discussion on our משנה, which says that one who sells a fetus to a non-Jew, though not permitted, frees it from בכורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach it on our משנה: 'and one who sells to him, even though he is not permitted...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא introduces another version of the same discussion. This line is a setup: it quotes the משנה that the next question will be about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'אף על פי שאינו רשאי' in our משנה say that selling a fetus is not allowed. That sets up the question of whether this fits רבי יהודה's view.

keyTerms.meaning: And some teach it (an alternate version)
Even though he is not permitted

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question. It is the same discussion told differently, starting from our משנה instead of from the question 'עובר לרבי יהודה מהו'.

phrases.english: And there are those who teach it on our mishna:
'And one who sells to him,'
phrases.notes: Sells the fetus of his donkey to a non-Jew.

phrases.english: 'even though he is not permitted.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins an alternate version of the whole discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Our משנה calls selling a fetus to a non-Jew 'not permitted'.

steps.title: Does our משנה disagree with רבי יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that our משנה does not follow רבי יהודה, who permits selling a broken animal. A fetus also cannot work, so he might permit it too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say our משנה is not like רבי יהודה? For we learned: רבי יהודה permits a broken animal!
steps.whatsHappening: In this version, the גמרא worries that our משנה's ban on selling a fetus clashes with רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה permits selling an animal that cannot work. A fetus cannot work now either, so maybe he would permit it. If so, our משנה, which forbids it, would not match his view. The next step answers this by pointing out that a fetus is in its natural state, while a broken animal is defective.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (a suggested conclusion, often rejected)
As we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: Shall we say our mishna is not like Rabbi Yehuda,
as we learned:
Rabbi Yehuda permits a broken animal!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises the challenge in the alternate version set up in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The fit between our משנה and רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה permits an animal that cannot work. A fetus cannot work, so he might permit it, against our משנה's 'not permitted'.

steps.title: Our משנה can follow רבי יהודה: a fetus is in its normal state
steps.stepSummary: Even רבי יהודה would forbid selling a עובר. A broken animal is defective, but a fetus is in its natural state.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say our משנה follows רבי יהודה. A broken animal is not in its normal state, but a fetus is in its normal state.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 10. Our משנה can follow רבי יהודה after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 said that a fetus cannot work, just like a broken animal, so רבי יהודה might permit selling it. The answer splits the two cases. A שבורה is damaged and outside its normal condition, but a עובר is exactly how a young animal is supposed to be, and it will work later. So רבי יהודה's leniency for a broken animal does not carry over to a fetus.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say (it fits this opinion too)
A broken, injured animal
Its normal way or natural state
A fetus, an unborn animal

steps.confusionAlert: A fetus also cannot work right now, so do not think it is the same as a broken animal. The difference is that a fetus is not defective. Its inability to work is natural and temporary.

phrases.english: You can even say it is Rabbi Yehuda
a broken animal — that is not its normal way
a fetus — that is its normal way
phrases.notes: A fetus is not defective. It will grow up and work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between the cases (broken vs. naturally immature)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A fetus cannot work, like a broken animal, so רבי יהודה would permit selling it.
steps.terutzMaskana: A broken animal is defective, while a fetus is in its natural state. So רבי יהודה forbids selling a fetus, and our משנה can follow him.

steps.title: Attempted proof from a ברייתא about giving an animal to a non-Jew
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי יהודה says that one who gives an animal to a non-Jew for care, 'though not permitted,' is fined. The גמרא suggests this means the fetus was forbidden to give.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יהודה says, if someone takes an animal from a non-Jew to raise and it gives birth, we assess its value, and he gives half its value to the כהן. And if someone gives his animal to a non-Jew to raise, even though he is not permitted, we fine him up to ten times its value, and he gives all its value to the כהן. Isn't this talking about the fetus?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that רבי יהודה really forbids giving a fetus to a non-Jew. That would support the answer in Step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case, the Jew owns only half the newborn, so only half is holy as a בכור and he pays half its value to the כהן. In the second case, the Jew gave the animal to the non-Jew, which he was 'not permitted' to do, so he is fined heavily. The גמרא suggests that the forbidden item was the fetus, since the money goes to the כהן because of the בכור. If so, רבי יהודה forbids handing over a fetus.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (a source is being brought as proof)
One who takes in an animal to raise for a share of the profits
An arrangement where one person raises another's animal and they split the profits
He is not permitted
We fine or penalize (a rabbinic penalty)

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different cases here. In the first, the Jew receives an animal from a non-Jew, and that is allowed. In the second, the Jew gives his animal to a non-Jew, and that is the forbidden case that gets the fine.

phrases.english: Come and hear: Rabbi Yehuda says:
one who receives an animal from a non-Jew to raise, and it gave birth —
we assess it at its value,
and he gives half its value to the Kohen.
And one who gives to him (the non-Jew) an animal to raise,
even though he is not permitted —
we fine him up to ten times its value,
and he gives all its value to the Kohen.
Is it not about the fetus?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to back up Step 11 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה forbids giving a fetus to a non-Jew.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי יהודה about giving an animal בקבלה to a non-Jew, 'though not permitted.'

steps.title: No, the prohibition is about the mother animal
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's 'not permitted' may refer to handing over the mother animal itself, not the fetus.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is talking about the animal itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof. The forbidden thing in the ברייתא could be giving over the large mother animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Giving a large animal to a non-Jew is forbidden by everyone. So the phrase 'not permitted' might be about the mother animal, and then the ברייתא tells us nothing about a fetus.

keyTerms.meaning: No (rejecting the suggested reading)
An animal, here the mother animal

phrases.english: No, it is about the animal (the mother).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only how the ברייתא is read, not its ruling.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The 'not permitted' could refer to the mother animal, which is forbidden anyway.

steps.title: But the ברייתא says 'its value' in the masculine
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא uses the masculine word דמיו, which points to the masculine עובר, not the feminine בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it says 'his/its value' (masculine)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rejection in Step 13 from the ברייתא's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בהמה is a feminine word, so 'its value' should be דמיה. The ברייתא says דמיו, which matches the masculine עובר. That suggests the ברייתא is about the fetus after all.

keyTerms.meaning: Its value (masculine form)
It teaches; this is what the source says

phrases.english: But it teaches 'its value' (masculine)!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the דחיה of Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the ברייתא is about the mother animal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The masculine wording fits the fetus, not the feminine animal.

steps.title: Change the reading to the feminine 'its value'
steps.stepSummary: Read the word as דמיה (feminine), referring to the mother animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Teach it as 'her value.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by changing the wording of the ברייתא to the feminine form.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא keeps its reading by correcting the text to דמיה. Now the fine is about the mother animal's value, and the proof from wording is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: Teach it (read the text) this way, an emendation
Her value (feminine form)

phrases.english: Teach (read) 'her value.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of Step 14.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The masculine wording proves the ברייתא is about the fetus.
steps.terutzMaskana: Read it as feminine, so it refers to the mother animal.

steps.title: But why would the money go to the כהן?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says all the value goes to the כהן. If it is about the mother animal, the כהן has no claim to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it teaches 'he gives all its value to the כהן.' If it is about the animal, what does the כהן have to do with it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a stronger challenge from the ברייתא's ending.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן gets money only because of a בכור, which is the fetus. The mother animal is not holy. So the payment to the כהן seems to prove the ברייתא is about the fetus, even with the wording changed.

keyTerms.meaning: A priest, who receives the firstborn animal
What is his business here; what does he have to do with it?

phrases.english: But it teaches 'he gives all its value to the Kohen,'
and if it is the animal — what does the Kohen have to do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא נוֹתֵן כָּל דָּמָיו לַכֹּהֵן קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new attack on the 'mother animal' reading, after the wording issue was answered.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the ברייתא is about the mother animal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The כהן only has a claim through the בכור (the fetus), so the ברייתא must be about the fetus.

steps.title: A pregnant animal given to fatten: the fine extends to the fetus
steps.stepSummary: The case is a pregnant animal given to a non-Jew to fatten. Because he is fined for the mother, he is also fined for the fetus, which goes to the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here we are dealing with a case where he gave a pregnant animal to fatten. Since we fine him for the animal, we also fine him for the fetus.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the כהן question by setting the ברייתא in a specific case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real sin was handing over the mother animal. Since the חכמים already fine him for that, they extend the fine to the fetus inside her, which is a בכור and goes to the כהן. So the ברייתא still does not prove that handing over a fetus alone is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here (setting a specific case)
Pregnant
To fatten it
Since (one thing applies, the other follows along)

steps.whyThisMatters: The fine on the fetus is only a side effect of the fine on the mother. So the ברייתא cannot tell us רבי יהודה's view on a fetus alone. That is why רב אשי needs a different proof.

phrases.english: Here what are we dealing with —
for example, where he gave a pregnant animal to fatten it,
so that since we fine him for the animal —
we fine him for the fetus too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the כהן challenge of Step 16, so the proof of Step 12 stays rejected.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (הכא במאי עסקינן) with a מיגו
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Payment to the כהן proves the ברייתא is about forbidding a fetus.
steps.terutzMaskana: The fine on the fetus comes only because of the forbidden giving of the mother.

steps.title: רב אשי proves it from רבי יהודה's reason
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה permits a broken animal because it cannot heal. So one that can heal is forbidden, and a fetus is like one that can heal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Come and hear. רבי יהודה permits a broken animal because it cannot be healed. This implies that if it can be healed, it is forbidden. And this fetus is also like something that can be healed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings a new and successful proof that רבי יהודה forbids selling a fetus.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's stated reason is that the broken animal can never become a working animal. That implies an animal that will be able to work is forbidden. A fetus will grow and work, so it falls on the forbidden side.

keyTerms.meaning: Permits
To be healed
This implies (an inference from the wording)
Is similar to; is compared to

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: Come and hear:
Rabbi Yehuda permits a broken animal,
because it cannot be healed.
This implies: if it can be healed — forbidden,
and this (fetus) too is like one that can be healed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא proof failed, רב אשי brings a new proof.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה forbids selling a fetus, so our משנה fits him.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה's reason for permitting a שבורה: it cannot be healed.

steps.title: Conclusion: רבי יהודה forbids selling a fetus
steps.stepSummary: The proof stands. רבי יהודה forbids selling a עובר, so our משנה can follow him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts רב אשי's proof and closes the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא proof was pushed away, but רבי יהודה's own reason settles the issue. A fetus is like an animal that can heal, so selling it is forbidden even according to רבי יהודה. Our משנה matches his view.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it; the proof is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה permits selling a broken animal only because it can never work. A fetus will work one day, so even he forbids selling it, and our משנה can follow him. The ברייתא about giving animals to a non-Jew did not prove this, because its fine on the fetus came only along with the mother.

phrases.english: Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the proof of Step 18.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהודה forbids selling a fetus to a non-Jew, so our משנה can follow him.

steps.title: New question: selling an animal only for its fetuses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about a Jew who sells a non-Jew only the rights to an animal's fetuses. It says the question can be asked according to both רבי יהודה and the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: if someone sold an animal only for its fetuses, what is the law? Ask it according to רבי יהודה, and ask it according to the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a brand-new question about selling only the rights to an animal's babies to a non-Jew. It also tells us it will explain the question according to each side of the earlier argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a Jew may not sell a large animal to a non-Jew. Here the Jew keeps the mother and sells only the fetuses, so we must ask whether that counts as a forbidden sale. The question works for both רבי יהודה, who permits a broken animal, and the רבנן, who forbid it. That is why the גמרא will now explain it from each side.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked before them: an unresolved question (בעיא)
He sold an animal for its fetuses: the buyer owns only the future babies
Let it be asked: the question applies according to this opinion
The Sages, who argue with רבי יהודה

steps.confusionAlert: The Jew is NOT selling the whole animal. He keeps the mother and sells only the rights to her fetuses. That is the whole point of the question.

phrases.english: A question was asked to them:
If he sold an animal for its fetuses, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He keeps the mother and sells only the fetuses to the non-Jew.

phrases.english: Ask it according to Rabbi Yehuda,
Ask it according to the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מָכַר בְּהֵמָה לְעוּבָּרֶיהָ, מַאי?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After proving that רבי יהודה forbids selling a fetus, the גמרא asks a new, related question: selling an animal only for its fetuses.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is it allowed to sell a non-Jew only the rights to an animal's fetuses, according to רבי יהודה and according to the רבנן?

steps.title: רבי יהודה's side: maybe forbidden because of confusion
steps.stepSummary: Maybe רבי יהודה permits only a broken animal, since no one will confuse it with a healthy one. A healthy animal sold for its fetuses might cause confusion, so he would forbid it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Ask it according to רבי יהודה: maybe he permits only a broken animal, because people will not get confused by it. But a whole animal, which can cause confusion, he forbids.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first way to look at the question according to רבי יהודה. Maybe he would forbid this sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה allowed selling a broken animal because everyone can see it is different from a healthy one. A healthy animal sold for its fetuses looks like any normal animal. People might think it is fine to sell a healthy animal outright. So the reason for his leniency may not apply here.

keyTerms.meaning: He only permitted up to here: his leniency is limited to this case
A broken (injured) animal that cannot do work
To be confused or mixed up with something else
A whole, healthy animal

phrases.english: Ask it according to Rabbi Yehuda:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָא שָׁרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda only permitted
in the case of a broken animal,
since it will not lead to confusion,
but a whole animal, which can lead to confusion —
he forbids.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן לָא קָא שָׁרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first side of the question according to רבי יהודה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is רבי יהודה's leniency based on the lack of confusion? If so, it would not reach a healthy animal sold for its fetuses.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's side: maybe permitted all the more
steps.stepSummary: Or maybe a קל וחומר applies. A broken animal leaves the Jew's hands completely and is still permitted. So a whole animal, where the Jew keeps the mother, should surely be permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe we say: a broken animal, which leaves him completely, is permitted. All the more so a whole animal, which does not leave him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side for רבי יהודה. Maybe he would permit this sale even more easily.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the focus is how much of the animal leaves the Jew's ownership. With a broken animal, the whole animal is sold, and רבי יהודה still allows it. Here the mother stays with the Jew, so by a קל וחומר it should be even more allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps: introduces the other side of a question
If this is so, then all the more so that: the form of a קל וחומר
It is cut off from him: it fully leaves his ownership

phrases.english: Or perhaps,
if a broken animal, which is fully cut off from him, is permitted,
then all the more so a whole animal
which is not cut off from him?

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִלְמָא, וּמָה שְׁבוּרָה דִּפְסַקָה מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite side to Step 21: a קל וחומר to permit.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי יהודה's leniency depend on how much leaves the Jew's ownership? If so, this case should be even more permitted.

steps.title: The רבנן's side: maybe permitted because the animal stays with the Jew
steps.stepSummary: Maybe the רבנן forbid a broken animal only because it leaves the Jew's hands completely. A whole animal sold only for its fetuses stays with him, so they might permit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Ask it according to the רבנן: maybe they forbid only a broken animal, since it fully leaves him. But a whole animal, which does not fully leave him, they permit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the רבנן and shows how the question works for them. For them, there is a possible reason to be lenient here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן forbid selling even a broken animal, because the whole animal goes to the non-Jew. In our case, the Jew keeps the mother and sells only the fetuses. So the reason the רבנן were strict may not apply, and they might permit it.

keyTerms.meaning: They forbid
They permit

steps.confusionAlert: Notice the reversal. For רבי יהודה, the question was whether he would become strict. For the רבנן, who are normally stricter, the question is whether they would become lenient here.

phrases.english: Ask it according to the Rabbis:
the Rabbis only forbade
a broken animal, which is fully cut off from him,
but a whole animal, which is not cut off from him —
they permit.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּיבְּעֵי לְרַבָּנַן: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָסְרִי רַבָּנַן אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both sides for רבי יהודה, the גמרא explains the question according to the רבנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the רבנן's strictness based on the animal fully leaving the Jew's ownership? If so, they might permit selling only the fetuses.

steps.title: Maybe the רבנן would forbid it even more
steps.stepSummary: The second side of the question about the רבנן: if they forbid a broken animal, which cannot be confused with a healthy one, they would surely forbid selling the fetuses of a healthy animal, which can be confused.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps the reasoning goes the other way. A broken animal will not be confused with a healthy one, and the רבנן still forbid selling it. So a whole animal sold only for its fetuses, which people will confuse with selling a healthy animal, should surely be forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second side of the question about the רבנן. It suggests a קל וחומר that would lead them to forbid the sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 23 the reasoning was that the רבנן might permit this sale, because the whole animal stays with the Jew. Here the logic flips. If the רבנן forbid even a broken animal, where confusion is unlikely, then a healthy animal, where confusion is likely, should be forbidden even more.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps (introduces the other side of a question)
A broken (badly injured) animal
A whole, healthy animal
To be confused or mixed up with something else
All the more so

steps.confusionAlert: Here the 'confusion' points the opposite way from Step 21. A healthy animal sold for its fetuses looks like selling a healthy animal outright. That is exactly the kind of sale that is forbidden.

phrases.english: Or perhaps: if a broken animal,
which people won't come to confuse, they forbid,
then all the more so a whole animal
which people will come to confuse.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִלְמָא: וּמָה שְׁבוּרָה דְּלָא אָתְיָא לְאִיחַלּוֹפֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second side of the question about the רבנן that Step 23 opened.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Would the רבנן forbid selling the fetuses of a healthy animal by a קל וחומר from a broken animal?

steps.title: A ברייתא suggests the רבנן's reason is the offspring
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that the רבנן's reason is confusion. A ברייתא shows them arguing to רבי יהודה that a broken animal can still be bred and give birth, which suggests their concern is the fetuses.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is the רבנן's reason really this concern about confusion? But a ברייתא teaches that they said to רבי יהודה: 'Don't people breed a broken animal, and it gives birth?' This suggests their reason has to do with the animal's offspring.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the starting assumption of Steps 23 and 24. It asks whether confusion is really the reason the רבנן forbid selling a broken animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole question assumed the רבנן worry about confusion. But in the ברייתא they point to the broken animal's offspring. That suggests their real concern is the fetuses. If so, selling fetuses to a non-Jew would obviously be forbidden according to them, and there would be nothing to ask.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא (introduces a challenge from a source)
They breed it (mate it with another animal)
And it gives birth
Apparently / this shows that
Its fetuses / offspring

phrases.english: And is the Rabbis' reason because of this?
But it was taught: they said to Rabbi Yehuda:
But don't they breed it, and it gives birth!
Apparently it is because of its fetuses.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְטַעְמָא דְרַבָּנַן מִשּׁוּם הָכִי הוּא? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption behind Steps 23 and 24 that the רבנן's reason is confusion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the רבנן forbid selling a broken animal because of confusion
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא shows the רבנן pointing to the animal's breeding and offspring. That implies their reason is the fetuses, not confusion.

steps.title: The offspring point was aimed at רבי יהודה's logic
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן were really saying: our reason is confusion. But you, רבי יהודה, permit a broken animal because it cannot heal and is like an animal sold for slaughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what they meant to tell him: 'Our own reason is that people will confuse it with a healthy animal. But you, why do you permit it? Because the animal cannot be healed, so you treat it like an animal sold for slaughter.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It explains that the רבנן's own reason is still confusion, and that they were now turning to examine רבי יהודה's reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן separate two things: their own reason, which is confusion, and רבי יהודה's reason for permitting. רבי יהודה treats a broken animal as if it were sold for slaughter, which is allowed, because it can never recover. This step sets up the רבנן's rebuttal of that comparison in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what they were saying to him (reinterprets a statement)
Our reason
You permit
To be healed
For slaughter

phrases.english: This is what they were saying to him:
Our reason is because people will come
to confuse it with a healthy animal,
but you, what is your reason for permitting?
Because it cannot be healed,
it is like one who sold it for slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 25 by reinterpreting the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the source: the offspring argument rebuts רבי יהודה's reasoning and is not the רבנן's own reason.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן forbid because of the offspring.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן forbid because of confusion. The offspring point only attacks רבי יהודה's comparison to an animal sold for slaughter.

steps.title: The broken animal is kept alive, not slaughtered
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן finish their rebuttal. A broken animal can still be bred and give birth, so the non-Jew will keep it alive rather than slaughter it. It is not like an animal sold for slaughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'But don't they breed it, and it gives birth? And since they breed it and it gives birth, the non-Jew will keep it around.'
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן finish rejecting רבי יהודה's comparison. This explains what their offspring argument in the ברייתא really meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה said a broken animal is as good as sold for slaughter. The רבנן answer that it can still be bred, so the non-Jew will keep it alive for its offspring. So the offspring point only shows the animal won't be slaughtered quickly. It is not the רבנן's own reason for forbidding the sale.

keyTerms.meaning: And since
He keeps it around / delays its slaughter

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן's own reason for forbidding a broken animal is confusion with a healthy animal. Their point about breeding was only aimed at רבי יהודה's comparison to an animal sold for slaughter. So the question about selling only the fetuses can still be asked according to the רבנן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer protects the original question from Steps 20–24. Because the רבנן's reason is confusion, both sides of the question about selling only the fetuses still make sense.

phrases.english: But don't they breed it, and it gives birth?
And since they breed it and it gives birth,
he will keep it around!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲלֹא מַרְבִּיעִין עָלֶיהָ וְיוֹלֶדֶת, וְכֵיוָן דְּמַרְבִּיעִין עָלֶיהָ וְיוֹלֶדֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reinterpretation begun in Step 26 by giving the רבנן's rebuttal of רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Completes the reinterpretation of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: A broken animal is not like one sold for slaughter, because the non-Jew will keep it alive to breed it. This is a rebuttal, not the רבנן's own reason.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's reply: a broken animal won't give birth
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה answers the רבנן: I'll worry about births when it actually gives birth. A broken animal cannot mate with a male. So the ברייתא is about confusion and the chance of breeding, not about selling fetuses, and gives no proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה said to them: When it gives birth, then we will worry. But it won't, since it does not accept a male.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes the ברייתא the גמרא has been reading: רבי יהודה rejects the רבנן's claim that a broken animal will be kept alive for breeding. With this, the ברייתא is fully explained and no longer proves anything about selling fetuses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן said the non-Jew will keep the broken animal for breeding, so it is not like an animal sold for slaughter. רבי יהודה replies that this is unrealistic because a broken animal will not mate. Their argument is only about whether the animal is like one bought for slaughter, so our question about selling fetuses stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: When it gives birth, meaning 'we'll deal with that when it happens'
Accepts a male, meaning it is able to mate

steps.whatToRemember: The broken-animal ברייתא is fully explained as a debate about confusion and slaughter. It does not settle whether the רבנן allow selling fetuses.

phrases.english: And he (רבי יהודה) said to them:
When it gives birth (then we will worry),
phrases.notes: He's brushing the question off: this isn't a real concern.

phrases.english: for it does not accept a male.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יהודה's counter-reply to the רבנן's argument in step 27, closing the reading of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the source: the ברייתא is about whether the animal is like one sold for slaughter, not about selling fetuses.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to show that the רבנן's concern is fetuses.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about confusion and breeding potential, so it gives no proof.

steps.title: Proof from the משנה: receivership has no 'not permitted'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries a proof from the משנה. Giving an animal to a non-Jew בקבלה (the non-Jew raises it and they split the offspring) is listed without the words 'even though he is not permitted'. So giving away partial rights to offspring seems allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: The משנה lists 'one who gives it to him in receivership,' and it does not say 'even though he is not permitted'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new proof from the wording of our משנה. Only the case of selling has the warning 'even though he is not permitted', and the case of receivership does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In קבלה the non-Jew gets a share of the offspring, which is a lot like selling the fetuses. Since the משנה does not warn against קבלה, the proof says that giving a non-Jew rights to the offspring is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear, the formula that introduces a proof
Receivership: giving an animal to someone to raise in exchange for a share of its offspring
Even though he is not permitted

phrases.english: Come and hear:
'and one who gives it to him (the gentile) in receivership'
and it does not teach:
'even though he is not permitted'!
phrases.notes: In the משנה, this phrase is attached only to selling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא gave no proof, so the גמרא tries a new source.
steps.raayaObject: Giving a non-Jew partial rights to the offspring (like selling fetuses) is permitted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's wording leaves out 'even though he is not permitted' for the case of קבלה.

steps.title: But partnership also lacks the warning, and it is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The משנה also leaves the warning off partnership, yet partnership with a non-Jew is forbidden according to אבוה דשמואל. He might owe an oath and swear by his idol, which violates 'לא ישמע על פיך'. So leaving out the warning proves nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by your logic, partnership is also listed without the warning. Is it also permitted? But אבוה דשמואל said: It is forbidden to make a partnership with a non-Jew, because he may owe an oath and swear by his idol, and the Torah says 'let it not be heard out of your mouth'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof by pointing to another case in the same משנה. That case also has no warning, yet we know it is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a missing warning meant 'permitted', then partnership would be permitted too. But אבוה דשמואל forbids it, so the missing warning cannot mean 'permitted'. The proof's method is broken.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning: turns the other side's logic against them
Partnership
The father of שמואל
'Let it not be heard out of your mouth', the verse forbidding causing a mention of idols

steps.confusionAlert: The Jew himself is not swearing by the idol. The problem is that he causes the non-Jew to swear by it. The verse is read to include that too.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
'one who partners with him', where it does not teach (the warning),
so too, is he permitted?
But didn't the father of Shmuel say:

phrases.aramaic: אָסוּר לְאָדָם שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה שׁוּתָּפוּת עִם הַגּוֹי,
phrases.english: It is forbidden for a person to make a partnership with a gentile,
lest he (the gentile) become obligated to him an oath

phrases.aramaic: וְנִשְׁבָּע לוֹ בְּשֵׁם עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁלּוֹ,
phrases.english: and he swears to him by the name of his idol,
and the Torah said:
'Let it not be heard out of your mouth'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the method of the proof in step 29.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the inference from the missing warning, not the משנה's ruling on firstborn status.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The same missing warning appears on partnership, which is known to be forbidden. So silence does not mean permission.

steps.title: The warning on selling covers the other cases too
steps.stepSummary: The warning written on selling also applies to partnership, and in the same way to receivership. So the משנה does not show that קבלה is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the משנה taught 'selling', and the same is true for partnership. So too, it taught 'selling', and the same is true for receivership.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how to read the משנה instead. The single warning on selling covers the other cases as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We are forced to say that the warning stretches to partnership. Once we say that, the same reading applies to receivership. The proof that קבלה is permitted falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: And the same law applies to
Selling
Receivership arrangement, the same as קבלה

phrases.english: Rather, (the תנא) taught selling,
and the same is true for partnership.
So too, he taught selling
and the same is true for receivership.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the reading of the משנה that follows from the rejection in step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the source: a stated detail stands for the whole list.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The warning applies only to selling, so the other cases are permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The warning on selling applies equally to partnership and receivership.

steps.title: Why did the משנה put the warning on selling?
steps.stepSummary: If the warning applies to all the cases, why did the משנה attach it specifically to selling?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is special about selling, that the משנה chose it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question about the new reading. It is setting up the final short answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the warning covers every case, it seems odd to write it on only one of them. The גמרא wants to know why selling was picked.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is different about
That he chose (to mention)

phrases.english: And what is different about selling, that he chose (it)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording choice that step 31's reading leaves open.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the warning is written on selling and not on the other cases.

steps.title: Selling is the main case
steps.stepSummary: Selling is the main and most common case, so the warning was written there and applies to the rest.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because selling is the main one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. The משנה put the warning on the main case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Selling is the clearest and most basic way of transferring the animal. The warning was placed on it, and the reader understands that it covers the other arrangements too.

keyTerms.meaning: The main or primary case

steps.whatToRemember: The missing warning on partnership and receivership does not make them permitted. The warning on selling, the main case, covers all of them. So the משנה gives no proof that selling fetuses is permitted.

phrases.english: Because selling is the main one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The warning sits on selling because selling is the main case.

steps.title: A new proof begins: רבי יהודה on a Jew who receives an animal from a non-Jew
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a ברייתא with תא שמע. רבי יהודה first rules on a Jew who raises a non-Jew's animal for a share of the offspring. If it gives birth to a firstborn, the Jew pays the כהן half its value.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יהודה says, if someone receives an animal from a non-Jew to raise it, and it gives birth, they assess its value, and he gives half of that value to the כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: After the earlier proof failed, the גמרא brings a new source. This first case sets up the background before the key line about the opposite case, where the Jew gives the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the Jew is the receiver, so he owns half the offspring. His half has קדושת בכור, so he redeems it by paying half its value to the כהן. The non-Jew's half does not become holy.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא is bringing a source to settle the question
One who receives an animal to raise in exchange for a share of the offspring
They assess it at its market value
Half its value, matching the Jew's half-share

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Rabbi Yehuda says,
one who receives an animal from a non-Jew
and it gave birth (to a firstborn)
they assess it at its value,
and he gives half its value to the kohen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from the משנה was rejected in steps 30-33, the גמרא brings a new source from a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: Whether a Jew may give a non-Jew partial rights to an animal's offspring

steps.title: The key line: giving an animal to a non-Jew to raise is not permitted and is fined
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה continues: one who gives his animal to a non-Jew בקבלה does something 'not permitted.' The חכמים fine him up to ten times its value, and he must give the full value to the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one who gives an animal to a non-Jew to raise, even though he is not permitted to do this, they fine him up to ten times its value, and he gives all of its value to the כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the heart of the proof. The ברייתא states outright that giving an animal בקבלה to a non-Jew is not permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 29 the גמרא wanted to learn from silence in the משנה, and step 30 rejected that. Here the warning is written explicitly: 'אף על פי שאינו רשאי.' The fine also shows how seriously this is taken: he must buy out the non-Jew's half even at up to ten times its value, so the whole animal becomes a בכור and all its value goes to the כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: One who gives his animal to a non-Jew to raise for a share of the offspring
Even though he is not permitted
They penalize him with a rabbinic fine
Up to ten times its value, to buy back the non-Jew's share

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. In step 34 the Jew RECEIVES from a non-Jew, which is allowed, and he pays half. Here the Jew GIVES to a non-Jew, which is forbidden, and he is fined and pays everything.
steps.whyThisMatters: Unlike the משנה, this ברייתא says outright that giving an animal בקבלה to a non-Jew is 'not permitted'. The גמרא is setting up a proof about giving a non-Jew rights to the offspring. But earlier on this amud (steps 13–17), this same 'not permitted' was read as being about the mother animal. So the proof is not settled yet, and its conclusion comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: And one who gives (an animal to a non-Jew) in receivership,
even though he is not permitted (to do so),
they penalize him up to ten times its value,
and he gives all of its value to the kohen.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַנּוֹתֵן בְּקַבָּלָה, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ רַשַּׁאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This continues the same ברייתא and supplies the line that actually makes the proof.
steps.raayaObject: Giving a non-Jew partial rights to offspring is forbidden
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה's words 'אף על פי שאינו רשאי' together with the fine

steps.title: The חכמים: any non-Jewish share in the animal exempts it from בכורה
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים disagree with רבי יהודה's payments. Any time a non-Jew has a share in the animal, it is fully exempt from בכורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: as long as the non-Jew's hand is in the middle, the animal is exempt from בכורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with the opinion of the חכמים. They hold that a partial non-Jewish share removes בכורה entirely, so no payment to the כהן is needed. The גמרא's use of this ברייתא to answer the question about selling only the fetuses continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה split the animal's holiness by ownership: half-holy when the Jew receives, and fully holy after the fine when the Jew gives. The חכמים hold that any non-Jewish partnership, even partial, exempts the whole animal from בכורה. The דין of בכורה itself still stands; this is a special outcome caused by shared ownership with a non-Jew.

keyTerms.meaning: And the Sages say: the opposing majority view
The non-Jew's hand is involved, meaning he has some share of ownership
Exempt from firstborn status

steps.whatToRemember: In this ברייתא, רבי יהודה says outright that giving an animal בקבלה to a non-Jew is not permitted, and he imposes a fine. The חכמים hold that any non-Jewish share exempts the animal from בכורה.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
as long as the hand of the non-Jew is in the middle,
phrases.notes: He owns part of the mother or the offspring.

phrases.english: it is exempt from firstborn status.
